# botyard_bot_schedule (Resource)

Manages one recurring schedule on a Botyard bot: when it fires (`cron`, `interval` or `rrule`) and what it does (`prompt` wakes the bot, `command` runs a command on its runtime).

The resource manages only the schedule it created or imported. Other schedules on the bot, including ones the bot created itself, are left alone; list them with the `botyard_bot_schedules` data source.

**Terraform owns `enabled`.** A schedule paused in the app, or auto-paused after `max_consecutive_failures`, shows as drift, and the next apply resumes it. Pause it from Terraform by setting `enabled = false`.

The next fire time changes on every read, so it is not stored here; read it from `botyard_bot_schedules`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A weekday check-in: wake the bot with a prompt at 09:00 Copenhagen time.
# conversation_id is left out, so Botyard creates a dedicated conversation and
# the resource adopts it.
resource "botyard_bot_schedule" "standup" {
  bot_slug = botyard_bot.assistant.slug
  title    = "Weekday stand-up"

  cron = {
    cron     = "0 9 * * 1-5"
    timezone = "Europe/Copenhagen"
  }

  prompt = "Post the stand-up summary for yesterday's merged PRs."
}

# A command on the bot's runtime every 15 minutes. Command schedules need the
# `schedule:schedule_command.create` / `.update` permission on the API key's
# role, on top of the schedule permissions.
resource "botyard_bot_schedule" "sync" {
  bot_slug                 = botyard_bot.assistant.slug
  title                    = "Upstream sync"
  max_consecutive_failures = 5 # auto-pause after 5 failures; the next apply resumes it

  interval = {
    interval_seconds = 900
    anchor           = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }

  command = {
    command           = "./scripts/sync.sh"
    cwd               = "jobs"
    timeout_seconds   = 600
    log_path          = "/home/openclaw/logs/sync.log"
    concurrency_group = "sync"

    # Values come from the Runtime Vault at each run; only the key path is here.
    secret_env = [{ name = "SYNC_TOKEN", secret_key_path = "sync.token" }]

    on_outcome = {
      failure = {
        retry = { max = 2, backoff_seconds = 60 }
        then  = { wake_bot = { message = "Sync failed with exit code {exit_code}:\n{log_tail}", include_log_tail = 20 } }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `bot_slug` (String) Slug of the bot the schedule belongs to. Changing it forces replacement.

### Optional

- `catchup_policy` (String) Fires missed while the bot was unavailable: `skip` (the default) drops them; `run_once_on_recovery` fires once when the bot is reachable again.
- `command` (Attributes) Run a command on the bot's runtime on each fire. Exactly one of `prompt` or `command`. Creating or switching to a command needs the `schedule:schedule_command.create` / `.update` permission on top of the schedule permissions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command))
- `conversation_id` (String) Conversation the schedule wakes into; it must be served by the same bot. When omitted, Botyard creates a dedicated conversation and this attribute adopts it. Changing it moves the schedule's wakes in place.
- `cron` (Attributes) Fire on a cron expression. Exactly one of `cron`, `interval` or `rrule`; switching kind updates in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cron))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the schedule fires. Defaults to `true`; a remote pause is planned back.
- `interval` (Attributes) Fire on a fixed period. Exactly one of `cron`, `interval` or `rrule`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interval))
- `max_consecutive_failures` (Number) Auto-pause after this many consecutive failures. `0` (the default) never auto-pauses.
- `prompt` (String) Wake message delivered to the bot on each fire. Exactly one of `prompt` or `command`.
- `rrule` (Attributes) Fire on an RFC 5545 recurrence rule. Exactly one of `cron`, `interval` or `rrule`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rrule))
- `skip_if_busy` (Boolean) Skip a fire, rather than count it as missed, when the conversation already has an active turn. Defaults to `false`.
- `title` (String) Human-friendly label. Removing it clears the label.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The schedule ID.

<a id="nestedatt--command"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command`

Required:

- `command` (String) Shell command to spawn. Do not redirect its output: the runtime captures stdout and stderr into `log_path` itself.

Optional:

- `concurrency_group` (String) Lock shared across this bot's command schedules. Omit for no lock.
- `cwd` (String) Working directory, relative to the workspace root. Omit for the root.
- `exit_code_labels` (Map of String) Display label per `exit_codes` key, e.g. `{"75" = "Waiting for input"}`. Single line, 1 to 40 characters, no leading or trailing whitespace.
- `exit_codes` (Map of String) Exit code (`0`..`255`, or `*` for any other) to `success`, `failure` or `deferred`. Defaults to `{"0" = "success", "*" = "failure"}`. Declaring the map replaces the default entirely. `deferred` needs a `window`.
- `log_path` (String) Absolute path the runtime writes the command's stdout and stderr to.
- `on_outcome` (Attributes Map) Routing per outcome, keyed by outcome (`success`, `failure`, `timeout`, `lost`, `missed`, `secret_unavailable`, `skipped_overlap`, `late`, `ok`, `not_ok`). Empty (the default) means success and skipped_overlap do nothing, and every other outcome wakes the bot and notifies the accountable human. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command--on_outcome))
- `output_path` (String) Absolute path named in the wake message. The platform never reads it.
- `overlap_policy` (String) What a fire does while its `concurrency_group` lock is held: `skip` (the default) or `queue` (needs a `concurrency_group`).
- `overridable_env` (List of String) Environment variable names a manual trigger may set for one run. Override values are stored in run history as plain text, so never use them for secrets.
- `secret_env` (Attributes List) Environment variables resolved from the Runtime Vault at each spawn. Values never pass through Terraform: each entry names a vault key path. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command--secret_env))
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Deadline per attempt. Omit for no deadline.
- `window` (Attributes) Run until success within each period: a `deferred` exit is rechecked every `recheck_seconds` until success, or until the window closes (outcome `late`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command--window))

<a id="nestedatt--command--on_outcome"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command.on_outcome`

Optional:

- `notify_humans` (Attributes) Notify humans. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command--on_outcome--notify_humans))
- `pause` (Boolean) Pause the schedule (sets `enabled` to false remotely; the next apply re-enables it).
- `retry` (Attributes) Retry before acting. With `retry`, put the actions under `then`. Only failure, timeout, lost, missed and secret_unavailable may retry. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command--on_outcome--retry))
- `then` (Attributes) Actions applied once retries run out. Only valid with `retry`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command--on_outcome--then))
- `wake_bot` (Attributes) Wake the bot with a message. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command--on_outcome--wake_bot))

<a id="nestedatt--command--on_outcome--notify_humans"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command.on_outcome.notify_humans`

Optional:

- `mode` (String) `on_change` (the default) notifies only when the outcome flips between ok and not ok; `every_run` notifies on every matching outcome.
- `recipients` (List of String) User IDs to notify. Empty (the default) notifies the conversation's accountable human.


<a id="nestedatt--command--on_outcome--retry"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command.on_outcome.retry`

Required:

- `max` (Number) Retries after the first attempt.

Optional:

- `backoff_seconds` (Number) Delay before each retry. Defaults to `0`.


<a id="nestedatt--command--on_outcome--then"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command.on_outcome.then`

Optional:

- `notify_humans` (Attributes) Notify humans. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command--on_outcome--then--notify_humans))
- `pause` (Boolean) Pause the schedule (sets `enabled` to false remotely; the next apply re-enables it).
- `wake_bot` (Attributes) Wake the bot with a message. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--command--on_outcome--then--wake_bot))

<a id="nestedatt--command--on_outcome--then--notify_humans"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command.on_outcome.then.notify_humans`

Optional:

- `mode` (String) `on_change` (the default) notifies only when the outcome flips between ok and not ok; `every_run` notifies on every matching outcome.
- `recipients` (List of String) User IDs to notify. Empty (the default) notifies the conversation's accountable human.


<a id="nestedatt--command--on_outcome--then--wake_bot"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command.on_outcome.then.wake_bot`

Required:

- `message` (String) Wake message. May use `{outcome}`, `{exit_code}`, `{label}`, `{attempt}`, `{log_tail}`, `{output_path}` and `{window_end}`. Write a literal brace as `{{` or `}}`.

Optional:

- `include_log_tail` (Number) Lines of `log_path` to quote into the wake. `0` (the default) quotes none; anything else needs `log_path`.



<a id="nestedatt--command--on_outcome--wake_bot"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command.on_outcome.wake_bot`

Required:

- `message` (String) Wake message. May use `{outcome}`, `{exit_code}`, `{label}`, `{attempt}`, `{log_tail}`, `{output_path}` and `{window_end}`. Write a literal brace as `{{` or `}}`.

Optional:

- `include_log_tail` (Number) Lines of `log_path` to quote into the wake. `0` (the default) quotes none; anything else needs `log_path`.



<a id="nestedatt--command--secret_env"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command.secret_env`

Required:

- `name` (String) Environment variable name. May not use the `BOTYARD_` or `LD_` prefix.
- `secret_key_path` (String) Runtime Vault key path; never a secret value.


<a id="nestedatt--command--window"></a>
### Nested Schema for `command.window`

Required:

- `duration_seconds` (Number) How long after each period start rechecks may run.
- `recheck_seconds` (Number) Delay between a deferred exit and the next check.



<a id="nestedatt--cron"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cron`

Required:

- `cron` (String) Cron expression, e.g. `0 9 * * 1-5`.

Optional:

- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone the schedule fires in, e.g. `Europe/Copenhagen`. Firing follows daylight-saving changes. Defaults to `UTC`.


<a id="nestedatt--interval"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interval`

Required:

- `interval_seconds` (Number) Period between fires, in seconds.

Optional:

- `anchor` (String) RFC 3339 instant the period is aligned to, e.g. `2026-01-01T09:00:00Z`. Omit to align to the Unix epoch.
- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone the schedule fires in, e.g. `Europe/Copenhagen`. Firing follows daylight-saving changes. Defaults to `UTC`.


<a id="nestedatt--rrule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rrule`

Required:

- `rrule` (String) Recurring RFC 5545 rule with at least two occurrences, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=MO`. May embed `DTSTART`.

Optional:

- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone the schedule fires in, e.g. `Europe/Copenhagen`. Firing follows daylight-saving changes. Defaults to `UTC`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Schedules are imported as <bot_slug>/<schedule_id>. List a bot's schedule IDs
# with the botyard_bot_schedules data source.
terraform import botyard_bot_schedule.standup my-assistant/2f0c3a9e-8d41-4b6a-9e57-1c2d3e4f5a6b
```
